note: Hypothetical inputs. Expected behaviours are proposed evaluator judgments, not author requirements.

cases.task: Whether to sell variable-cost work (AI generation, research, messages, jobs) as unlimited, pure pay-as-you-go, or a plan allowance in credits with top-ups, and how to rate each action so heavy users don't erase margin.

inputs_hypothetical.business: Booking app for salons with AI reply drafting

expected_behaviors: Notes 70% average margin hides ten customers at about -$50 contribution each
Proposes an allowance whose full use costs at most $28 plus priced top-ups or a fair-use cap for the heavy tail
Asks for comprehension testing and a balance display
Labels the 70–80%/10% concentration figure as the author's experience, not a benchmark
hard_failures: Raising price for all customers as the only fix
Recommending unlimited usage on the strength of expected falling AI costs
Inventing the customer's cost distribution

cases.task: Which billing unit fits a business whose product does work for the customer: per person, flat subscription, usage allowance, per completed job/workflow, or per result.

inputs_hypothetical.business: Two-person lead-gen agency for local contractors
inputs_hypothetical.attribution: appointments booked through client's own phone line, not tracked

expected_behaviors: Flags that attribution is not reliable and cash buffer is thin
Recommends base retainer plus a per-appointment bonus with call tracking, or a fixed package until tracking exists
States the outcome model's preconditions explicitly
hard_failures: Endorsing pure pay-per-result without an attribution method
Citing the guest author's 'outcome pricing will win' as evidence for this business

cases.task: How to structure tiers and add-ons, and which lever to add when a single flat offer leaves no room for customers to pay more as they get more value.

inputs_hypothetical.observation: a third of clients ask for payroll and monthly calls

expected_behaviors: Suggests payroll as an add-on (different need, costly to serve) or a premium tier with calls

Keeps base package delivering full bookkeeping
Labels the 15–25% uptake range as one author's software experience
hard_failures: Moving core bookkeeping into the premium tier
Promising Kyle's +15% revenue as an expected result

cases.task: Which free-access configuration a self-serve product should test, and which conversion reference applies to it.
expected_behaviors: Case A: proposes a reverse-trial test with end-date disclosure, downgrade to free and a cost cap, and explains why

cases.task: How to describe and price an AI-enabled feature or service on landing and pricing pages.

cases.task: Did the change cause harm that blocks shipping, and may the test stop early for it?

expected_behaviors: treatment 1.2% vs control 0.5%: +0.7 points, +140% relative
Fisher exact p = 0.1418, not significant, but 1.2% > 1.0% bound with 1,000 sends -> guardrail breached
blocks ship wording even if replies rose
stop rule 'pause if unsubscribes pass 1%' is accepted, not flagged as peeking
hard_failures: calls the unsubscribe rise 'not significant, so safe'
ships on replies alone
lint rejects the harm stop as peeking
